You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue report shows an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException arising at Base64.encode, specifically at line 502 in Base64.java, indicating a problem related to data being written to the buffer array beyond its length. The Base64InputStream.read() method repeatedly calls the overloaded read(byte[], int, int) method to fetch encoded data. Inside the Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int) method, when new data is needed, a buffer is allocated (size 4096 or 8192 bytes depending on encoding mode), incoming data is read, and then Base64.encode is called.

In the Base64.encode method (line 444 onwards), when encoding, the buffer is extended via resizeBuffer() as needed. The resizeBuffer() method doubles the buffer size when it needs to grow, copying existing data across. The encoding logic then writes encoded byte values sequentially into the buffer at position 'pos' and increments pos.

The ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException with an index of 2 indicates that in some case, the buffer size is too small and pos is incremented beyond buffer length, or a race or state condition results in array access beyond buffer length.

Potential root cause:
- The buffer array may sometimes not be resized properly before writes near the end of the buffer.
- The checks before writing to buffer, namely the "if (buffer == null || buffer.length - pos < encodeSize) { resizeBuffer(); }" at line 485 in encode, might be insufficient or faulty under certain boundary conditions, causing the buffer to be too small when writing the 2nd or 3rd byte of the encoding group, leading to out-of-bounds access.
- Because the failure occurs after many thousands of reads (10920 successful reads), it suggests a subtle buffer sizing or boundary growth bug gradually manifesting.

This diagnosis aligns exactly with the issue report and test behavior: multiple sequential byte reads triggering incremental buffering and encoding steps, eventually triggering the buffer overflow problem during Base64 encoding in Base64InputStream.

Next step: To confirm, we could verify exact buffer length and pos increments and edge cases around resizing calls in Base64.encode. Also, checking if encodeSize is correct and consistent is relevant.

Therefore, the root cause appears to be a buffer resizing bug or off-by-one boundary error in Base64.encode and the related resizeBuffer method, causing array overrun during encoding multiple sequential bytes.

The test triggers this by streaming many single-byte reads through a Base64InputStream that encodes data and exposes the bug as a program crash.

This concludes the step-by-step diagnosis based on the test, bug report, and method inspection.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
